What a capsule says of its data: where each file came from, the schema of its tables, summaries that show drift later, the environment of the run, and commitments.

Each section is one help page: what its functions are for, and the example
of the page as it runs. `?name` gives the arguments and the value in full.

## The data record of a capsule

`nqdata()`, `nqdadd()`, `nqdput()`, `nqdcheck()`: A capsule's data record, `noqtis.data.json` in its folder, says where each data file came from, the schema of its CSV files, summaries that show drift later, and the steps and checks made with it (the format `noqtis-data-1`). It is a file of the capsule like any other: seal the folder (`nqseal()`) after changing the record, and the seal covers it. The record is canonical JSON, the same bytes the `noqtis` tool and every other binding write.

```{r nqdata}
d <- file.path(tempdir(), "cap")
dir.create(file.path(d, "data"), recursive = TRUE)
writeLines(c("x,y", "1,a", "2,b"), file.path(d, "data", "a.csv"))
nqdadd(d, "data/a.csv", url = "https://example.org/a.csv")
nqdata(d)
nqdcheck(d)
unlink(d, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Sources: where a file can be fetched, and the portals' resolvers

`nqdaddr()`, `nqdverify()`, `nqdfield()`, `nqdrslv()`, `nqdreply()`, `nqdwayback()`: A source of the data record names where its file came from. These functions make no network request: they say what to fetch and read what came back, as the noqtis src command does (the C functions are `nqdaddr(3)`).

```{r nqdaddr}
rs <- '{"base":"https://data.example.org","id":"abcd-1234","kind":"socrata"}'
nqdrslv(rs)
nqdreply(rs, charToRaw('{"id":"abcd-1234","name":"Crimes"}'))
nqdwayback("http://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://example.org/a.csv")
```

## Pin and check the schema of CSV files

`nqschema()`, `nqschk()`: `nqschema()` reads each CSV file (RFC 4180) and returns its schema as JSON: the columns, the narrowest type each fits (`bool`, `int`, `real`, `date`, `text`; a leading zero keeps a code text), whether each has missing values (`""` and `NA`), the number of rows, and with `ranges` each number and date range. With `put`, it records them in the data record instead. `nqschk()` checks the files against the schemas the record pins: header, types, missing values, ranges, sets, row counts and rules (add rules with `nqdput()`).

```{r nqschema}
d <- file.path(tempdir(), "sch")
dir.create(d)
writeLines(c("id,when", "1,2024-01-02", "2,2024-02-29"),
           file.path(d, "a.csv"))
nqschema(d, "a.csv")
nqschema(d, "a.csv", put = TRUE)
nqschk(d)
unlink(d, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Summaries that show drift later, and the check against them

`nqdpin()`, `nqdrift()`: `nqdpin()` records in the data record summaries of each CSV file, of a fixed size whatever the file's: for a numeric column a quantile sketch of 1,001 points (every distinct value when there are at most 1,001), the population stability index's decile bins and first-digit counts; for any other column the counts of its 1,000 most frequent values. `nqdrift()` compares each summarised file (or `current`, a later copy) with its summary: the two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, PSI and Jensen-Shannon divergence, the chi-square test of homogeneity, and Benford's first-digit test. The tests and their error are defined in the manual page `noqtis-drift(1)`; on the test vectors they match R's `stats::ks.test()` and `stats::chisq.test()` to 1e-9.

```{r nqdpin}
d <- file.path(tempdir(), "dft")
dir.create(d)
write.csv(data.frame(x = round(stats::qnorm(ppoints(200)), 6)),
          file.path(d, "a.csv"), row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
nqdpin(d, "a.csv")
nqdrift(d)
unlink(d, recursive = TRUE)
```

## More of the data record: parse, synthetic data, calibration, chunks

`nqdparse()`, `nqdschk()`, `nqdsyn()`, `nqdcal()`, `nqdchunk()`, `nqdpiece()`: `nqdparse()` reads JSON text as a data record, as noqtis data check reads one, and returns it in canonical form (an error says what is wrong and where). `nqdschk()` checks the CSV file of one `"schemas"` element against it. `nqdsyn()` writes a synthetic stand-in for a CSV file from the schema the record pins for it (the same bytes for the same seed) and records it as a synthetic source; real data is never replaced. `nqdcal()` calibrates the drift warnings of a file's summary on files known not to have drifted from it, so `nqdrift()` then warns only beyond what they showed. `nqdchunk()` records the SHA-256 of each run of `chunk` bytes of a large file, and `nqdpiece()` checks a piece of that file (the bytes from `off` on) against them, reading only the piece.

```{r nqdparse}
d <- file.path(tempdir(), "dx")
dir.create(file.path(d, "data"), recursive = TRUE)
writeLines(c("id,x", "1,0.5", "2,1.5", "3,2.5"), file.path(d, "a.csv"))
nqdparse('{"format":"noqtis-data-1"}')
s <- nqschema(d, "a.csv")
attr(nqdschk(d, s), "ok")
nqdput(d, "schemas", sub('"a.csv"', '"data/s.csv"', s, fixed = TRUE))
nqdsyn(d, "data/s.csv", seed = 7)
readLines(file.path(d, "data", "s.csv"))
nqdpin(d, "a.csv")
invisible(nqdcal(d, "a.csv", file.path(d, "a.csv")))
writeBin(as.raw(rep(0:255, 8)), file.path(d, "big.bin"))
invisible(nqdchunk(d, "big.bin", chunk = 1024))
p <- tempfile()
writeBin(as.raw(rep(0:255, 4)), p)
attr(nqdpiece(d, "big.bin", p, off = 1024), "ok")
unlink(c(d, p), recursive = TRUE)
```

## Record the environment of a run

`nqdenv()`, `nqdpkgs()`: `nqdenv()` records in the data record's `"env"` the environment of a run, as noqtis env does (the platform, the noqtis version, the locale and time zone, the SHA-256 of the lock files at the top of `dir`, the random number generator and its seed), and fills the runtime: R, its version, and the packages. `nqdpkgs()` lists the packages: by default those loaded in this session, each with its version and where it came from (`"CRAN"` or the repository its description names, `"github"` and the like for a remote install, `"base"` for R's own, else `"local"`). Nothing is fetched.

```{r nqdenv}
d <- file.path(tempdir(), "env")
dir.create(d)
writeLines("{}", file.path(d, "renv.lock"))
head(nqdpkgs())
e <- nqdenv(d, seed = 42)
substr(e, 1, 60)
unlink(d, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Commitments, citation and the report of a capsule

`nqdcommit()`, `nqdreveal()`, `nqdcite()`, `nqdreport()`: `nqdcommit()` commits to some content (a randomisation list, an analysis plan) in the data record, as noqtis commit does: the record gets the SHA3-256 of the content under a fresh 32-byte secret salt, which is returned; keep the salt and the content out of the capsule until the reveal, and seal the capsule (with a timestamp) so the commitment is dated. Without the salt the record says nothing of the content. `nqdreveal()` finds the commitment that content and salt match, comparing every recorded digest in constant time. `nqdcite()` writes how to cite the data, from the record's `"cite"`. `nqdreport()` checks the capsule and its record and writes a report of both, as noqtis report does.

```{r nqdcommit}
d <- file.path(tempdir(), "cm")
dir.create(d)
writeLines("x", file.path(d, "a.txt"))
s <- nqdcommit(d, "arm A: 1, 4\narm B: 2, 3\n", kind = "randomisation")
nqdreveal(d, "arm A: 1, 4\narm B: 2, 3\n", s)
nqdreveal(d, "something else", s)
nqdput(d, "cite", '{"title":"T","authors":["A. Author"],"year":2026}')
cat(nqdcite(d))
k <- nqkeygen("ML-DSA-44")
nqseal(d, k$sk, k$pk, "ML-DSA-44")
cat(nqdreport(d, k$pk, format = "txt"))
unlink(d, recursive = TRUE)
```
